gate.ref: The scheduled inf-accounts-v2-daily run at cron(22 13 * * ? *) = 13:22Z. NOT to be forced. TWO independent reasons, and COO's is the stronger one I had missed: (1) an ad-hoc invoke REWRITES snapshot_date=2026-07-13 IN PLACE -- that partition ALREADY EXISTS (873 rows, written 13:22:50Z today) and accounts_v2 uses a FIXED key per date, so a re-emit OVERWRITES BYTES. That is the in-place-partition-rewrite hazard we documented this morning (6 of 69 accounts_v2 partitions rewritten after their own snapshot_date). (2) this lambda calls the ORION VENDOR API, so an ad-hoc run is agent-initiated vendor egress AND an ad-hoc validation run (NEVER#4's spirit: validate on the SCHEDULED run's artifacts, never one you manufactured to validate against). NOTHING IS BLEEDING: the gold chain is HELD (INF_GOLD_DISPATCH_HOLD applied, both trigger rules DISABLED -- COO re-verified), the fold switch is OFF, and nothing is served. There is no reason to buy 20 hours with an in-place rewrite. THE ACCEPTANCE READ IS COO'S, NOT MINE (the verifier is not the do-er).
